content-bible §3b: 'Never imply physical offices in the location metros.' There is ONE office, at the canonical NAP. The safe geography framing is 'from our Las Vegas office'. WHAT THIS RULE TARGETS, stated exactly because the previous pattern got it wrong: a claim that the firm HAS OFFICES LOCATED IN the coverage metros — a plural physical presence. It does NOT target a SINGLE office SERVING those metros, which is the mandated truth. ⚠ PATTERN RE-AUTHORED 2026-08-12 — THE PREVIOUS PATTERN WAS A LIVE, BUILD-BREAKING FALSE-BLOCK. It matched the mere CO-OCCURRENCE of an office noun — optionally SINGULAR — within 40 characters of in/across/throughout and within 30 more of metros/markets/cities. So it fired on 'One Las Vegas office serving clients across US metros.', which is VERBATIM what briefs/about.md line 30 mandates the about page say, and on 'From our Las Vegas office, check in one screen whether your market is covered.' Swept across the 26 briefs it hit 10 lines, and the classification is stated exactly rather than rounded: TWO hits landed directly on copy the page is MANDATED to carry — about.md:30 (the verbatim §4 geography sentence) and our-locations.md:13 (the Outcome line) — and those are the unambiguous false-blocks. FOUR more landed on lines that MANDATE the permitted numberless coverage sentence and ban the alternatives in the same breath, where the match fell on the ban clause: index.md:55, industries-contracting.md:91, industries-hvac.md:91 and industries.md:97. Only FOUR were pure ban-notice rows: about.md:63, guarantee.md:278, index.md:210 and our-locations.md:73. bannedContent hits are hard errors in build.mjs lint(), audit.mjs and the block-banned-content write hook, so the rule made mandated brief copy unshippable — CLIENT-RULES-SCHEMA.md §2's named worst failure class, and this file's own standing warning at _rationedClaims_notes. THE RETIRED PATTERN, RECORDED VERBATIM SO THE HISTORY IS NOT LOST RATHER THAN ONLY DESCRIBED: '\boffices?\b[^.!?]{0,40}\b(in|across|throughout)\b[^.!?]{0,30}\b(metros?|markets?|cities)\b|\b(\d{2}) (offices|locations)\b'. THE NEW PATTERN REQUIRES BRAND-ATTRIBUTED OR LOCATIVE PLURALITY, never co-occurrence. Six alternatives: (1) the brand possessing PLURAL offices — 'our offices', 'we have offices', 'the firm's offices' — which is false on its face because there is exactly one; (2) 'offices' asserted as located IN a coverage noun (metros / metro areas / metropolitan areas / markets / cities) or in one of the 24 published coverage metros BY NAME, or claimed 'nationwide' / 'coast to coast'; (3) the brand asserting a COUNT of offices, locations or branches ('we operate 25 locations', 'our 12 US offices'); (4) a per-metro presence claim — 'our Portland office', 'our Miami team' — which briefs/our-locations.md line 81 and briefs/index.md line 55 ban by name; (5) 'locally based in', also named at our-locations.md line 81; (6) an UNATTRIBUTED count of offices or branches ('25 offices', 'twenty-five offices', '12 regional offices'), which restores the coverage the retired pattern's second limb had at '\b(\d{2}) (offices|locations)\b' — dropping it in the rewrite would have been a fail-OPEN regression introduced while fixing a fail-CLOSED one. NOTE WHAT ALTERNATIVE 6 DELIBERATELY OMITS: 'locations'. An unattributed count of LOCATIONS is not banned, because in this bundle that word belongs to the CLIENT's premises — briefs/industries-dental.md line 112 and industries-medical-spa.md line 97 both mandate asking 'how many locations the practice runs'. A count of locations is caught only under alternative 3, where the brand attributes it to itself. LAS VEGAS IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the metro-name list: it is the one real office and its name must never trip this rule. TWO GUARDS, both lookbehinds, both present to protect true copy. The HONEST-DENIAL guard keeps negated statements clean — 'We have no offices in the metros we cover', 'We do not have offices in Miami, Denver or Seattle', and briefs/industries.md line 97's 'Never any implication of offices in any metro' — because denying a branch network is exactly what this brand's honest copy does. The OTHER-PARTY guard keeps the CLIENT's premises clean — 'your offices in three cities' and briefs/industries-dental.md line 112 / industries-medical-spa.md line 97, whose mandated line asks 'how many locations the practice runs'. ENGINE REQUIREMENT, STATED BECAUSE IT IS NEW TO THIS FILE: both guards are LOOKBEHIND assertions, and this is the first rule here to use one. Every declared consumer is a Node ESM script — scripts/revision-rules.mjs, build.mjs lint(), block-banned-content.mjs, audit.mjs — and V8 has supported variable-length lookbehind since Node 8.3, so the dependency is already satisfied. A consumer written in an engine WITHOUT lookbehind (Go RE2, older Safari, Python re without the regex module) will throw on compile rather than silently mis-match; if one is ever added, this rule must be re-authored, not skipped. FLAGS ARE LEFT AS AUTHORED at 'gi' — see _rationedClaims_notes.flags_are_deliberately_non_global, which records that a /g RegExp reused across pages via .test() keeps lastIndex and can silently skip a hit. That hazard is PRE-EXISTING on this entry and is not repaired here, because the consumers that would be affected live in a build tree that does not exist yet and the change could not be verified. Flagged, not fixed. VERIFIED 2026-08-12 by reading this pattern back OFF DISK, compiling it and running it: 42 of 42 cases behaved as specified, 0 failures. CLEAN on about.md:30 verbatim, our-locations.md:13 verbatim, 'One Las Vegas office serving clients across US metros.', 'From our Las Vegas office, check in one screen whether your market is covered.', the mandated numberless coverage sentence, and the denial and client-premises cases above. FIRES on 'We have offices in 25 US metros.', 'Our offices across Phoenix, Denver and Miami', 'with offices in Miami, Denver and Seattle', 'Our Portland office', 'our Miami team', 'We maintain offices throughout the major markets we serve.', 'offices nationwide', 'We operate 25 locations across the country.', 'our 12 US offices' and 'We are locally based in Denver.' ZERO matches on mandated or descriptive copy, down from six. Both residues are authoring rules for the build's P11 content pass, enforced by the ⚠OWNER PLACEHOLDER wording on every coverage-carrying brief — do not read this entry as complete mechanical coverage.
